C-EVIDENCE-DISCRIMINATION.Summary: Ship a lint warning that refuses a CloseEvidence Command whose text has no failing path: allowlist by command shape, polyglot defaults derived from the shipped language adapters, a .ngrace-lint.json additive escape, and an --explain text that states the cheap-class limit. Completeness is already linted; power is not.

Goals.Goal: Emit a new sibling lint code change.close-evidence-undiscriminating at warning when a complete CloseEvidence Command's flattened text matches no default discriminating shape and no configured extra prefix. Keep change.close-evidence-incomplete and change.close-evidence-and-satisfied unchanged in code, severity, and message family.

Allowlist by command shape, never a denylist of binaries. git diff without --exit-code warns; git diff --exit-code does not. The flag decides. Defaults are polyglot and derived from the five shipped adapters (LANGUAGE_ADAPTERS) plus this product's lint driver plus the git shape D26 measured. A hardcoded set of this repository's package.json scripts is rejected.

Config-driven escape: new .ngrace-lint.json key closeEvidenceCommandShapes, an array of non-empty strings, each a flattened command prefix, additive to the defaults, unable to remove a default. Closest key-shape precedent is codeExtensions (additive to a built-in set). Closest acknowledgement precedent is unverifiedLanguages.

ngrace lint --explain change.close-evidence-undiscriminating states the cheap-class limit: well-known runners have non-assertive modes (pytest --collect-only, cargo test --no-run, go test -run matching nothing) and git diff --exit-code over the wrong paths still exits 0. A green rule is not evidence that the harder check happened.

README.md documents closeEvidenceCommandShapes next to the existing config keys, and the skillTextLines measurement cell if a SKILL.md rewrite moves the published figures. examples/ is unchanged; no user-visible CloseEvidence surface there.

Matching a runner token does not inspect non-assertive flags. pytest --collect-only and cargo test --no-run therefore do not warn. That is the cheap class; the --explain text must say so.

Resolving package.json, Makefile, or justfile to decide whether a script exits non-zero. Owner: D26 / C-PHASE-RULE-PIN rejected reading B. "A script designed to exit non-zero" is an intent claim the linter cannot check.

AcceptanceCriteria.AC-SIBLING-WARNING: A complete CloseEvidence Command whose flattened text matches no default shape and no configured prefix emits change.close-evidence-undiscriminating at warning from validateSpecAcceptanceCriteria, as a sibling of change.close-evidence-incomplete. git log --format=%B warns. true warns. git diff without --exit-code warns. An empty or missing Command still emits change.close-evidence-incomplete at error, not the new warning. change.close-evidence-and-satisfied is unchanged. Failure conditions: new code is an error; denylist of the git binary rejects git diff --exit-code; incomplete Commands are reclassified as the new warning.
AcceptanceCriteria.AC-DEFAULT-SHAPES: Flattened Commands that carry every required token of a default shape do not emit the new warning: bun test …, a Command containing token vitest, a Command containing token jest, node --test …, pytest …, python -m unittest …, python3 -m pytest …, dart test …, go test …, cargo test …, bun run ngrace lint --path . --fail-on warnings, bun ./src/grace.ts lint --path . --fail-on warnings, git diff --exit-code … -- CHANGELOG.md. pytest --collect-only and cargo test --no-run also do not warn (cheap class). Failure conditions: bun test warns; git diff --exit-code warns; a this-repo package.json script name is required for a default match.
AcceptanceCriteria.AC-CONFIG-ESCAPE: closeEvidenceCommandShapes in .ngrace-lint.json is an array of non-empty strings, additive to defaults, and cannot remove a default. A Command whose flattened text equals an entry or starts with the entry followed by a space does not warn. bun run validate:examples warns with no config and does not warn when that string is a configured prefix. A non-array or empty-string entry emits config.invalid-close-evidence-command-shapes at error. An unknown config key still emits config.unknown-key, and that message names closeEvidenceCommandShapes. Failure conditions: config replaces defaults; detector reads package.json to honour the prefix; malformed values are ignored.
AcceptanceCriteria.AC-NO-TRANSITIVE-RESOLVE: The detector does not read package.json, Makefile, or justfile. bun run ./scripts/validate-marketplace.ts and bun run validate:teaching-surface warn unless those exact prefixes are configured, even if the underlying script exits non-zero on failure. Failure conditions: detector opens those files; a package-script name is treated as discriminating by default.
AcceptanceCriteria.AC-EXPLAIN-LIMIT: ngrace lint --explain change.close-evidence-undiscriminating (and bun ./src/grace.ts lint --explain of the same code) prints an exact catalog guide whose explanation states that the rule catches only the cheap class, and names pytest --collect-only, cargo test --no-run, go test -run matching nothing, and git diff --exit-code over the wrong paths as cases a green rule does not prove. The code is exact-guided and not on PREFIX_COVERED_LEGACY_CODES. Failure conditions: explanation claims the command was shown to fail; cheap -class examples omitted; code is prefix-allowlisted.
AcceptanceCriteria.AC-REPO-ESCAPE: After the rule lands, this repository's .ngrace-lint.json lists the three opaque prefixes already in the CloseEvidence corpus (bun run ./scripts/validate-marketplace.ts, bun run validate:examples, bun run validate:teaching-surface) so those existing Commands do not warn, while the same Commands warn in a fixture that omits the key. Defaults still do not include those prefixes. Failure conditions: prefixes added to the default table; existing corpus Commands warn at this root after landing; fixture without the key stays silent.
